quoted_clause: ≈ 10 s planning round (Ch 4: retrieval ~0.12 s + prefill 1.08 s + decode 7.5 s, rounded) for the canonical non-agentic round; grows with turns
observed: The listed components sum to 8.70 s, not ≈10 s.
evidence: 0.12 + 1.08 + 7.5 = 8.70 s. If W_e2e is intended to be 10 s, the missing ~1.3 s component is not listed.
root_cause: Stale or incomplete decomposition of the end-to-end planning round.
correction: Change the value to ≈9 s, or add the missing queue/orchestration/retrieval components so the listed terms sum to the printed W_e2e.
acceptance_test: A reader can sum the parenthetical components and obtain the printed W_e2e within rounding, or see all components included.

page_hint: Ch 17 §4, bullet on the 25 ms/token TPOT budget and sensitivity band
quoted_clause: Sizing at the 25 ms budget is a tighter internal target than the 40 ms SLO pole, so name the sizing pole once and state it once: sizing at the SLO pole gives ~31 hosts, and a measured per-step time from a Chapter 14 benchmark should replace the model before committing hardware.
observed: The 31-host number is the 25 ms policy working count; at the 40 ms SLO pole with Table 17-1 policy the count is 47 working / 48 total. The sentence omits the policy and can imply 31 hosts at the SLO pole.
root_cause: Conflation of the full-utilization KV screen at the SLO pole with the policy-derated count at the 25 ms budget.
correction: State explicitly that the 40 ms SLO pole gives ~31 hosts only as a full-utilization KV screen; under Table 17-1 it gives 47 working / 48 total. The headline 31/32 is at the 25 ms budget.
acceptance_test: No sentence implies that 31 hosts satisfies the 40 ms SLO pole under the 70% x 95% policy.

quoted_clause: at batch 100 ~23,900 tok/s per GPU. At 200 rps × 100 output tokens the aggregate output-token demand is 20,000 tok/s — the same per-GPU scope — which needs a batch large enough to clear it on one serving GPU; after bandwidth, verify compute/KV headroom at the required batch. The host count is set by λ·O / (per-host token rate), not by KV residency; one host here serves the model on one GPU, so the per-host rate is the per-GPU rate above.
observed: The 23,900 tok/s figure is weights-only. For a 7B model with a 600-token context, KV traffic can be significant, so the one-host conclusion is conditional on KV/compute verification, but the sentence can be read as asserting one host suffices.
evidence: If a 7B full-MHA model has κ ≈ 0.524 MB/token, B = 100, context = 600, KV per step ≈ 31.4 GB; total traffic ≈ 45.4 GB; rate ≈ 3.35 TB/s / 45.4 GB * 100 ≈ 7,380 tok/s, below 20,000 tok/s.
root_cause: A weights-only roofline is presented near a one-host conclusion without making the condition explicit.
correction: State that 23,900 tok/s is a weights-only roofline; add the KV term or explicitly condition the one-host claim on KV/compute headroom at the required batch.
acceptance_test: The counter-scenario does not assert one host is sufficient without a KV-inclusive check.

quoted_clause: uses NGINX with least-connections (power-of-two-choices) load balancing
observed: Least-connections and power-of-two-choices are different load-balancing algorithms; the parenthetical can imply they are the same.
evidence: Power-of-two-choices samples two servers and selects the less loaded one; least-connections tracks connection counts. They are related but not identical.
correction: Say least-connections or power-of-two-choices, or specify which one is intended.
acceptance_test: A reader does not infer that the two algorithms are identical.

quoted_clause: The 120/250/300/800 ms values are illustrative per-request latencies for a short-prompt routing scenario ... not the ~8.6 s service time of the 9.5K-token canonical RAG request ... The cost column, by contrast, is computed on the canonical 9.5K-token request
observed: The same 70/20/10 routing split is costed on 9,500-token requests but latency-gated on short-prompt TTFT values. A 9,500-token request cannot have 120 ms TTFT on a 70B FP16 8xH100 host because prefill alone is ~1.08 s.
evidence: Ch 17 canonical prefill is 1.08 s for 9.2K input tokens. §18.3.4 explicitly says the 120/250/300/800 ms values are short-prompt TTFT, not the canonical 9.5K service time.
root_cause: Two request classes are mixed in one routing example: canonical 9.5K cost and short-prompt latency.
correction: Separate the cost example (canonical 9.5K requests) from the latency gate (short-prompt requests), or use canonical TTFT/service times for the routed 9.5K requests.
acceptance_test: The request class used for cost and the request class used for latency are identical or explicitly separated; no 9.5K request is checked against a 120 ms short-prompt TTFT.

quoted_clause: Consolidate when: workload profile overlap ≥70%, latency tolerance ≥300 ms, and cost differential >30% ... the latency criterion is met against the ≤500 ms interactive threshold of §18.3.4, not the ~200 ms chat tolerance quoted in §18.2 — L̄ ≈ 247 ms clears 500 ms and exceeds 200 ms, so consolidation is eligible for a ≤500 ms per-request chat budget and would fail a 200 ms budget.
observed: The bullet uses a 300 ms criterion, but the justification uses a 500 ms threshold. The relationship is not explained.
evidence: Lbar = 247 ms, which is below both 300 ms and 500 ms. If the governing threshold is 500 ms, the 300 ms criterion is not the one being checked.
root_cause: Misaligned design criterion and chapter threshold.
correction: Align the criterion to the threshold actually used, e.g. latency tolerance at least the chapter's interactive threshold (≤500 ms), or explain that 300 ms is a worked-example margin.
acceptance_test: The consolidation criterion and latency check use the same threshold or explicitly state which governs.

page_hint: Ch 18 §3.3, Placement assumption, per-tier C and N
quoted_clause: Under the dedicated placement the no-policy pair falls below the single-model fleet (20 vs 21) while the policy pair is marginally above it (32 vs 31) — the ledger narrows rather than reverses.
observed: 32 is the dedicated total with per-group spares; 31 is the single-model working count. Same-basis comparison: dedicated working 29 vs single-model working 31 (below), or dedicated total 32 vs single-model total 32 (equal).
evidence: Dedicated per-tier policy: 8-bit ceil(240.8/(20*0.665)) = 19, MoE ceil(68.8/13.3) = 6, FP16 ceil(34.4/11.305) = 4; working 29, spares 3, total 32. Single-model working 31, total 32.
root_cause: Mixing working and total host counts in the comparison.
correction: State the basis: dedicated working 29 vs single-model working 31; with per-group N-1 spares both totals are 32, or adjust the sentence to compare the same quantity.
acceptance_test: The comparison uses the same quantity (working or total) on both sides.

page_hint: Ch 18 §3.1, Hardware capacity mapping table, 8-bit rows
quoted_clause: 4 (70 GB weights + 24.9 GB FP16 KV = 94.9 GB > 80 GB per GPU; FP8 KV still 82.5 GB)
observed: 94.9 GB is the total 1-GPU infeasibility check, not a per-GPU requirement for the 2-GPU instance. For 2 GPUs, 94.9 GB total is ~47.5 GB/GPU before reserve.
evidence: 70 + 24.9 = 94.9 GB > 80 GB for one GPU; 94.9 / 2 = 47.45 GB < 80 GB for two GPUs.
root_cause: Ambiguous use of per GPU in a total-pool fit test.
correction: Rephrase to distinguish 1-GPU infeasible from 2-GPU feasible, e.g. 1xH100 infeasible: 70 + 24.9 = 94.9 > 80; 2xH100 feasible: 94.9 total, ~47.5 per GPU before reserve.
acceptance_test: A reader does not infer that each GPU needs 94.9 GB.

quoted_clause: the tier needs ≥2 GPUs (160 GB, 3 concurrent) or must be declared short-prompt-only. Minimum placement is ⌈(70 + 24.89)/80⌉ = 2 GPUs.
observed: The 3-concurrent claim uses (160 - 70) / 24.89 without subtracting a runtime/workspace reserve. The canonical 8xH100 budget subtracts 64 GB; if a comparable reserve applies to 2-GPU placement, concurrency may be lower.
evidence: (160 - 70) / 24.89 = 3.61, floor 3. If a 64 GB reserve is subtracted, (160 - 70 - 64) = 26 GB, which supports only 1 concurrent canonical request.
root_cause: Missing reserve assumption for non-canonical 2-GPU placement.
correction: State the reserve assumption for 2-GPU instances; if no reserve is subtracted, justify it; if a reserve is subtracted, recompute the concurrency.
acceptance_test: The 3-concurrent claim has an explicit memory-reserve assumption.

quoted_clause: Latency-per-token determines interactive vs. batch placement.
observed: The routing gate and SLO check use per-request service latency (TTFT for short-prompt), not per-token latency. The canonical per-token TPOT budget is 25 ms, but the 120/250/300/800 ms values are per-request.
evidence: §18.3.4 defines per-request service latency; Table 18-1 uses per-request latency; the canonical TPOT budget is a per-token quantity.
root_cause: The design-principle metric does not match the operational gate.
correction: Change the principle to per-request service latency (or per-token latency for long generations), or use per-token values in the gate.
acceptance_test: The latency metric in the routing gate matches the design principle.

quoted_clause: W(3) = 17.70 s is on the same model-side basis — it excludes only the per-invocation step (3 × 120 ms = 360 ms), the 3 × 133 ms = 399 ms tool leg being already inside both figures — so the two differ by the guardrail term: ≈ 17.60 s model-side + guardrail — not the completed T = 3, whose terminal synthesis call the fallback never makes
observed: The fallback full service time is 17.40 s model-side + 0.20 s guardrail = 17.60 s, which is 0.10 s below completed T=3 W = 17.70 s. The difference is not solely the guardrail term. Also, W(3) has four model invocations, so 3 x 120 ms is not the full per-invocation step exclusion unless the synthesis step is intentionally excluded.
evidence: Fallback = failed 3-turn attempt (30,195 input, 195 output, 3 tool legs) + single-shot (9,200 input, 300 output): (30,195/9,200)*1.08 + 0.025*195 + 3*0.133 + 1.08 + 0.025*300 = 8.82 + 8.58 = 17.40 s; +0.20 = 17.60 s. Completed T=3 = 17.70 s. Difference = 0.10 s, caused by the fallback final prefill being 2,595 tokens shorter than the completed synthesis prefill.
root_cause: Muddled comparison of fallback and completed T=3 service times.
correction: Rewrite to state the 0.10 s difference and its cause; clarify whether per-invocation step is included or excluded for all four calls in both W(3) and the fallback.
acceptance_test: The numerical relationship between fallback and completed T=3 is explicit and correct.

page_hint: Ch 19 §4, Multi-step reasoning cost, W formula and Lagent discussion
quoted_clause: The tool/retrieval leg here uses Chapter 17's ~133 ms/turn rate; the chapter's own T·L_agent (~220 ms/turn) is the orchestration-only incremental overhead, a different quantity (see below).
observed: Lagent includes 120 ms per-invocation step, but the W formula includes only 133 ms tool/retrieval per turn. If the step occurs while KV is resident, W undercounts full service time; the text does not justify excluding it.
evidence: W(T) = prefill + decode + T*133 ms; Lagent = 120 + 100 = 220 ms. For T=3, omitted step could be 360-480 ms depending on whether the synthesis call is counted.
root_cause: Inconsistent treatment of non-model overhead in the orchestration metric versus the fleet-sizing service time.
correction: State whether lambda_step is included in W; if excluded, explain that it is not KV-holding or is absorbed in measured prefill; if included, add the appropriate number of 120 ms steps and update W and host counts.
acceptance_test: A reader can see exactly which overhead terms are in W and why Lagent differs.

quoted_clause: Plan and Decide are two evaluations of one model invocation per cycle (the Decide verdict is the next cycle's Plan input); the capacity model counts one LLM call per turn plus the terminal synthesis call (§4).
observed: The preceding list says Decide is The model evaluates whether the observation resolves... after Observe, which sounds like a separate model call. The following sentence says Plan and Decide are two evaluations of one model invocation, which is inconsistent with the sequence.
evidence: The capacity model T+1 calls implies no separate Decide call; Decide is the next cycle's Plan decision.
root_cause: State-machine wording conflates a state with a model invocation.
correction: Rewrite: Decide is not a separate model call; it is the next cycle's Plan decision. Each turn has one model invocation that either calls a tool or terminates, plus a final synthesis call.
acceptance_test: A reader can map the four states to T+1 model invocations without inferring an extra Decide call.

quoted_clause: It added, at the median T = 1, ~220 ms of orchestration latency (on top of an ~8.6 s base generation), but improved answer correctness ... full service time rises from ~8.6 s to W(1) ≈ 11.52 s (+34%) and processed tokens to 2.52×, against an estimated +22% correctness
observed: 2.52x is the distribution-weighted processed-token multiplier per submitted request (23,927 / 9,500), not the median T=1 value. At median T=1, processed tokens are 19,630 / 9,500 ≈ 2.07x.
evidence: §8 ledger T=1 total is 19,630 tokens; distribution-weighted total is 23,927 tokens per submitted request.
root_cause: Ambiguous attachment of at the median T = 1 to the 2.52x figure.
correction: Clarify: at the median T=1, service time rises to 11.52 s; across the distribution, processed tokens are 2.52x per submitted request.
acceptance_test: A reader does not infer that median T=1 processed tokens are 2.52x.

page_hint: Ch 19 §4, Multi-step reasoning cost, Lagent vs W discussion
quoted_clause: the chapter's own T·L_agent (~220 ms/turn) is the orchestration-only incremental overhead
observed: Lagent = lambda_step + lambda_tool, so it includes tool backend time, not only orchestration. Calling it orchestration-only can mislead.
evidence: The formula is Lagent = 120 ms + 100 ms; the 100 ms term is tool backend round-trip.
correction: Use non-model per-turn overhead or orchestration + tool overhead instead of orchestration-only.
acceptance_test: The label matches the components included in Lagent.
